original_question: Consider a Hamiltonian system with a center at the origin and Hamiltonian H(x,y) = H_{2n}(x,y) + H_m(x,y), where H_{2n} and H_m are homogeneous polynomials of degrees 2n and m with m > 2n. Does the period annulus of the origin have at most one critical period?
target_in_paper: Section 3.1, Problem 12, in the subsection A class of Hamiltonian systems. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct problem family and almost the exact official wording: the Hamiltonian is of the form H(x,y)=H_{2n}(x,y)+H_m(x,y), with m>2n, H_{2n} and H_m homogeneous of degrees 2n and m, the origin is assumed to be a center, and the question is whether the period annulus of the origin has at most one critical period. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is in the real planar Hamiltonian setting; to make the question stand-alone, one should state the associated Hamiltonian system explicitly as \dot{x}=\partial H/\partial y and \dot{y}=-\partial H/\partial x, with x,y real variables and H_{2n}, H_m understood as real homogeneous polynomials in R[x,y]. This ambient setting is implicit in the surrounding discussion of smooth planar autonomous systems. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The universal quantifier is implicit in the paper and should be made explicit: the question asks whether every such Hamiltonian system, provided the origin is a center, enjoys the one-critical-period property. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

A fully stand-alone version should define the period annulus of the origin as the maximal set covered by the family of periodic orbits ending at the origin, and define critical periods as zeros of T'(s), where T is the period function and s is typically the energy parameter. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The nearby context narrows the genuinely open range: the paper states that the answer is already known to be yes when m >= 4n - 2, so what remains open there is 2n < m < 4n - 2. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
The paper also records the simplest remaining case, namely H(x,y)=H_4(x,y)+H_5(x,y). ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

There is no nilpotency condition or other extra singularity assumption in this problem; beyond homogeneity and degree restrictions, the only qualitative hypothesis is that the origin is a center. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
refined_question: For every real planar Hamiltonian system \dot{x}=\partial H/\partial y, \dot{y}=-\partial H/\partial x having a center at the origin and Hamiltonian H(x,y)=H_{2n}(x,y)+H_m(x,y), where n>=1, m>2n, and H_{2n},H_m in R[x,y] are homogeneous polynomials of degrees 2n and m respectively, is it true that the period function T(h) on the period annulus of the origin, parametrized by the energy h, has at most one critical period, i.e. at most one value h for which T'(h)=0?
justification: Section 3 first introduces the notions of period annulus, period function, and critical periods. Immediately afterward, Section 3.1 states Problem 12 in exactly the H_{2n}+H_m form targeted by your draft. The sentence right after Problem 12 sharpens the open part by noting that the affirmative answer is already known for m >= 4n - 2, leaving only 2n < m < 4n - 2 to investigate, and it identifies H_4+H_5 as the simplest remaining case. So your draft is very close to the paper, but a paper-faithful stand-alone version should explicitly state the real planar Hamiltonian equations, the universal quantifier, and the definition of critical period via the period function. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
